task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/iss0444-poller-schema-availability.md exactly: (1) claim_due_timer_ids/2 gains a narrow rescue matching error in Postgrex.Error, testing error.postgres.code in [:undefined_table, :undefined_schema] (match?/2 guard, mirroring pin_rebind.ex:376-393's precedent), logging via Logger.warning/2 (alerts.ex:588-592's message-plus-keyword shape) and returning [] on match, reraising with __STACKTRACE__ otherwise; no @spec/@type change. (2) run_retention_sweep/1 gains the identical rescue shape at its own call site (not inside EventStore.archive/1, per the design's re-verified 1-production-caller finding), resolving to {:error, {:schema_unavailable, tenant_schema}} on match -- its existing @spec already covers {:error, term()}. (3) Confirm poller.ex's moduledoc needs no edit (its 'poll_and_fire/1 never raises, so no redundant rescue here' statement was already true in intent, becomes true in fact once this fix lands -- verified no edit needed). (4) Write tests reproducing ISSUE-FIXER's own real repro (claim_due_timer_ids/2 against a genuinely-absent tenant schema returns [] instead of raising) plus the identical case for run_retention_sweep/1, plus a Poller.handle_info/2 blast-radius test proving one registered-but-physically-absent schema does not crash the tick for other schemas, in both relative orderings. Mutation-test both rescue clauses (remove, confirm real crash, restore, confirm pass).

result.summary:
Implemented exactly per the approved design (§1-§4), no deviation, no scope creep.

1) lib/letflow/scheduler.ex: added `require Logger` to the module head (grep-confirmed absent before this change). claim_due_timer_ids/2's existing `Repo.all(query, prefix: tenant_schema)` (its only statement that can raise -- the query-building pipeline above it is pure Ecto.Query composition) now sits inside a `rescue error in Postgrex.Error ->` clause: `match?(%Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: code}} when code in [:undefined_table, :undefined_schema], error)` gates a `Logger.warning("scheduler: tenant schema unavailable, skipping timer poll for this tick", schema: tenant_schema, reason: :schema_unavailable)` call followed by `[]`; the `else` branch is `reraise error, __STACKTRACE__`. Return type is unchanged ([Ecto.UUID.t()]), matching the design's explicit 'no type widening' decision -- poll_and_fire/1's own body needed zero changes (it already handles an empty list from a normal empty-poll tick identically). run_retention_sweep/1 gets the byte-identical rescue shape at its own call site around `EventStore.archive(prefix: tenant_schema, retention_days: retention_days())` -- same match?/2 guard, same log call (message text 'skipping retention sweep for this tick' per the design's own §4 wording, same schema:/reason: metadata keys), resolving to `{:error, {:schema_unavailable, tenant_schema}}` on match (its existing @spec `{:ok, EventStore.archive_result()} | {:error, term()}` already covers this, confirmed by reading the actual @spec -- zero type change), reraising otherwise.

2) poller.ex moduledoc: confirmed via direct read (lines 30-35) that its 'poll_and_fire/1's own contract already guarantees it never raises, so no redundant try/rescue here' statement needs no edit -- per the design's own §1 conclusion, this was already true in intent and becomes true in fact once this fix lands; the architecture it describes is exactly what this fix restores, not something it changes. No edit made to poller.ex.

3) Tests added, following this codebase's own 'ExUnit.CaptureLog, no mocking library' convention:
   - test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs: 3 new describe blocks (claim_due_timer_ids/2, poll_and_fire/1, run_retention_sweep/1), each constructing a genuinely-never-provisioned schema name via a helper (`"tenant_" <> (Ecto.UUID.generate() |> String.replace("-", ""))` -- passes tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's format regex, backs no physical CREATE SCHEMA), asserting the new no-raise return value and that the Logger.warning/1 line fires (captured via ExUnit.CaptureLog).
   - test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs: a new fixture, registered_but_unprovisioned_schema_name!/0, builds a real Tenant + Registration row pair directly (NOT TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1, which always provisions physically) -- reproducing the exact real-world trigger backfill.ex's own moduledoc names ('Registration row exists but its physical schema no longer exists'). Two blast-radius tests drive Poller.handle_info(:tick, state) directly with this bad schema registered BEFORE vs AFTER a real, due-timer-bearing schema is provisioned (both orderings, per the design's §6 test-approach note that Enum.each's abort-on-raise pre-fix depended on ordering) -- both assert the real schema's timer still fires and the tick returns normally. A third test does the identical check for run_retention_sweep/1 with retention explicitly enabled (retention defaults disabled, per @default_retention_enabled false).

4) MUTATION-TESTING DISCIPLINE (both rescues), run for real:
   - claim_due_timer_ids/2's rescue removed (backed up scheduler.ex first): mix test test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs -> 5 real failures, all with an actual uncaught `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 42P01 (undefined_table)` in the failure output (not a silent assertion mismatch) -- exactly the 5 tests depending on this rescue (3 direct scheduler_test.exs tests + 2 poller_test.exs blast-radius tests, since the retention blast-radius test's tick also runs the timer-poll loop first). Restored from backup, diff confirmed byte-identical, recompiled clean.
   - run_retention_sweep/1's rescue removed: mix test -> 2 real failures (the direct run_retention_sweep/1 test + the retention blast-radius test), each with an actual uncaught `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 42P01 (undefined_table) relation \"...events\" does not exist` originating from EventStore.compute_archive_target_event_ids/2. Restored from backup, diff confirmed byte-identical, recompiled clean.

VERIFICATION (all run for real, in the foreground, this environment has a working toolchain via asdf -- `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` puts mix/elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 on PATH):
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`: clean, 'Generated letflow app', no warnings.
- `mix format` on lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs, test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs; `mix format --check-formatted` on all three (plus poller.ex, unedited) afterward: clean.
- `mix test test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs`: Result: 20 passed.
- `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`: Result: 16 passed.
- `mix test test/letflow/scheduler_req188_test.exs`: Result: 7 passed (recurring-timer/retention regression, unaffected).
- `mix test test/letflow/event_store_test.exs`: Result: 28 passed (archive/1's own ~9 call sites, confirmed unaffected -- this fix never touches archive/1 itself).
- Combined regression run (all 4 files together): Result: 71 passed.

Self-review checklist: no state-transition SHAPE changed (poll_result()'s @type is unchanged per the design's own §2 decision), so README.md's ASCII diagram is unaffected. No migration added. process_instance.ex not touched (this codebase's scheduler is a plain context module, not a :gen_statem). scheduler_test.exs:578-579's own pre-existing claim_due_timer_ids/2 length/1 assertions re-run and still pass (verified directly in the 20-passed run above, no modification made to that describe block). No new abstraction, no config layer, no supervision-strategy change.
result.routing: Route to REVIEWER (OTP idiom/scope gate) -- SECURITY-REVIEWER is not required per ISSUE-FIXER's own step-01 assessment (internal background-sweep resilience fix, no new API surface, no tenant-isolation boundary touched), re-confirmed here: this change only decides what happens when a boundary that already exists at the Postgres schema level is crossed by an operational anomaly (a raise -> a caught, logged, degraded-but-safe outcome). REVIEWER should confirm: (a) the rescue's placement (inside claim_due_timer_ids/2 and run_retention_sweep/1, not poller.ex, not EventStore.archive/1) matches this codebase's own 'rescue at the exact site of the risky I/O' idiom (pin_rebind.ex precedent) as the design's §1 argues; (b) the narrow match?/2 guard (both :undefined_table and :undefined_schema, re-raising everything else) is the right scope, not a bare `rescue _`; (c) the Logger.warning/2 shape matches alerts.ex:588-592's precedent as intended, not backfill.ex's bare-string shape. TEST-DESIGNER's own gate follows once REVIEWER passes, per WF-03's normal sequencing, though test coverage per the design's §6 test-approach notes is already implemented and passing here.

gate_history.notes: Final re-check (rework_count 1) PASS -- fabricated 'archive/1 has several other callers' claim removed and replaced with an independently re-verified 1-production-caller/9-test-call-site fact; all other sections byte-identical to the prior PASS pass.
